title: KV cache coherency & staleness-waveform evaluator for semantic drift detection
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Objective:
Create an automated evaluator and pipeline that attributes semantic output drift to KV/prefix cache coherency and 'staleness' (age) of cached KV states. We need a deterministic, repeatable signal that flags when cache reuse materially changes downstream generation quality and to gate config/model rollouts when that signal exceeds defined thresholds.

Scope:
- Instrument runtime to emit per-request cache metadata: hit/miss, hit_age_ms, hit_generation_token_index, cached_kv_version, eviction_count.
- Build a corpus and harness that runs controlled A/Bs: cold (cache disabled/cleared) vs warm (cache enabled and allowed to hit) vs aged-warm (allow hits with artificially increased hit_age).
- Produce metrics that combine token-level divergence (aligned edit distance), semantic shift (embedding cosine delta), and task-specific score regressions (e.g., accuracy for QA, functional tests for code).
- Provide visualization (staleness-waveform: time-series of semantic delta as a function of hit_age and token-position) and a scalar rollback_score used by rollout gates.

Success criteria:
- Pipeline produces stable signals reproducible within ±3% across 10 reruns on the canonical 5k prompt corpus.
- Able to detect deliberate cache-induced semantic changes with F1 ≥ 0.9 (synthetic adversarial cases).
- Gate blocks model/config rollouts when rollback_score > 0.12 and task metric loss > 2% on monitored prompts.

Approach / Implementation plan:
1) Instrumentation (ENG runtime): add lightweight telemetry hooks to emit cache event tuples to a Kafka topic. Fields: request_id, model, variant, route, cached_kv_version, hit_flag, hit_age_ms, hit_pos_index. Start with a feature flag (kv-stats-v2).
2) Corpus & harness (Evals infra): curate 5,000 prompts across categories: system prompts (10%), multi-turn chat (40%), code (20%), factual QA (20%), edge-case instructions (10%). Generate adversarial prefix permutations to surface brittleness.
3) Job runner: for each prompt, run three modes (cold, warm, aged-warm) across N=3 seeds. Collect responses, embeddings (sentence-transformers), log-probs, and token alignments.
4) Metrics: compute token-aligned edit ratio, embedding cosine delta, per-task metric delta, and an aggregate rollback_score = 0.6 * embedding_delta + 0.3 * token_edit_ratio + 0.1 * task_delta (configurable weights).
5) Visualization & gating: add a Console dashboard panel per-route showing staleness-waveform heatmap and a gating webhook for CI/CD that rejects deployments if the aggregated rollback_score exceeds threshold.

Test plan:
- Unit tests for telemetry shim and event schema validation.
- Synthetic regression tests: introduce a controlled KV corruption in staging to verify F1 detection.
- A/B runs in shadow mode for the next Dedicated release to collect baseline distribution.

Rollout plan:
- Stage 1: Run offline nightly jobs against hosted-model catalog to produce baseline distributions (1 week).
- Stage 2: Enable in-console shadow gating (notifications only) for two high-traffic routes.
- Stage 3: Enable active CI gate for runtime-1.24 canary rollouts.

Runbook (on detect):
- If rollback_score > threshold and task metric loss > configured SLA, trigger canary rollback and create incident INC-2026-14.
- Triage steps: compare cached_kv_version differences, inspect hit_age distribution, run per-prompt replay to local instance with kv-disabled.

Artifacts & links:
- Design spec (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/CACHE/KV+Coherency+Eval
- Dataset S3: s3://redwood-inference-evals/kv-coherency/2026-02-corpus-v1
- PR for runtime telemetry: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1209
- Prototype notebook: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/kv-coherency-proto

Notes / trade-offs:
- We rely on embedding deltas to capture semantics; embeddings can be noisy across model variants and quantization. Mitigation: normalize deltas by baseline variance per model and include a model-specific calibration step.
- Telemetry volume can be large; we will sample 1:10 by default and ramp up for specific routes.

Longer-term:
- Explore integrating a lightweight on-request hit-sanity check that validates cached KV fingerprints before reuse (cheap checksum) and falls back on miss if mismatch suspected.
- Extend to private deployments as a blackbox-runner using local logs and an offline harness.
